summary: Backend-only testing of the new 'one email/phone per referral code' enforcement across BOTH platform (POST /api/subscriptions/create-order) and Money Masters (POST /api/subscriptions/money-masters/create-order) checkout flows. Wrote 8 pytest tests in /app/backend/tests/test_referral_once_per_user.py covering: (1) block by same email different phone, (2) block by same phone different email, (3) fresh email+phone succeeds with correct 10% discount applied, (4) per-code scoping (same blocked user + different code succeeds), (5) regression - no referral_code still works, (6) admin CRUD list, (7) admin create+deactivate propagates to validate endpoint, (8) Money Masters flow blocks parent when their own account email/phone was previously redeemed under the same code (cross-plan-type, code-based match). All 8/8 passed on first run against the live backend using the production REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Setup used direct MongoDB inserts (payment_status='completed' fake subs, prefixed subscription_id='sub_qatest_*') and cleaned up in an autouse teardown fixture (also deletes test referral codes, MM test batch, and any qa_referral_* pending subs).
critical_code_review_comments: _check_referral_not_already_redeemed correctly filters out empty identifiers from the $or clause (avoids false-positive match on blank subscriber_email/phone). Verified via the 'no_referral_code_still_works' regression test.

Enforcement is consistently placed AFTER _resolve_referral_discount and BEFORE razorpay order creation in both create_order and create_money_masters_order — no payment is ever attempted when the block triggers.

Match is code-based (referral_code == code.upper()) so the block correctly spans across plan_types (platform single_parent, two_parents, and money_masters all share the subscriptions collection) — verified by test_mm_blocked_when_parent_identifiers_already_redeemed which seeds a plan_type='single_parent' completed sub and blocks a subsequent money_masters order using the same code.

Minor nit: email normalization uses .strip().lower() in platform create-order but only .lower() in MM (user.get('email') || '').lower(); if a parent's DB email has stray whitespace it could technically miss. Not blocking, and current DB records are clean.
